title: Anyone But You
about: Two people who can't stand each other pretend to be a couple at a destination wedding in Sydney.
cue: Serve the snacks when the wedding party heads out on the harbour.

    StartersHuntsman in the pants harbour prawnsChilled cooked prawns on ice with lemon and spicy cocktail sauceHow to make it500g cooked prawns2 lemons4 tbsp mayonnaise2 tbsp tomato saucehot sauce, a dash8 cups crushed icePile crushed ice onto a platter and arrange the prawns on top with lemon wedges.Mix the mayonnaise with tomato sauce and hot sauce.Serve in a bowl beside the prawns.Sydney meat piesMini beef mince pies with puff lids, served with tomato sauceHow to make it500g beef mince1 brown onion1 tbsp plain flour250ml beef stock2 sheets of shortcrust pastry2 sheets of puff pastry1 egg, beaten100ml tomato sauceDice the onion and brown with the mince.Stir in the flour and stock and simmer until thick, then cool.Cut the shortcrust into rounds and line a muffin tin. Fill with the mince and top with puff lids.Brush with egg and bake at 200°C until golden.Serve with tomato sauce.Opera House oysters with eschalot dressingThe wedding party taking in the Sydney Harbour viewsHow to make itAs written, serves 4Freshly shucked Sydney rock oysters on crushed ice with a sharp red wine vinegar and eschalot dressing, cracked pepper and lemon wedges.Finely dice 2 eschalots and mix with 80ml red wine vinegar, a pinch of sugar and plenty of cracked black pepper.Leave 15 minutes.Pile crushed ice onto a large platter.Check 24 freshly shucked oysters for shell grit and loosen each from its shell.Sit them on the ice with the dressing in a small bowl and a teaspoon, plus 2 lemons cut into wedges.Serve straight away.Sausage rolls with tomato sauceUnwritten comes baby potatoes4 barramundi fillets, skin on2 tbsp olive oil60g butter1 lemon, juiced, for the pan sauce1 lemon, cut into wedges, for serving2 tbsp capersBoil the potatoes until tender and crush lightly.Pan fry the barramundi in the olive oil, skin side down, until crisp, then flip briefly.Add butter, lemon juice and capers to the pan and spoon over the fish.Serve with the potatoes and lemon wedges.Rosemary lamb cutlets with potato saladThe wedding weekend in SydneyHow to make itAs written, serves 4Frenched lamb cutlets marinated in garlic, rosemary and lemon, grilled pink over high heat, with a warm potato salad of mustard, capers and herbs.Marinate 12 lamb cutlets in 3 tbsp olive oil, 2 crushed garlic cloves, 1 tbsp chopped rosemary and lemon zest for 30 minutes.Boil 1kg halved chat potatoes 15 minutes until tender.Whisk 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp red wine vinegar, 2 tsp wholegrain mustard and 1 tbsp capers.Toss through the warm potatoes with parsley and sliced spring onion.Grill the cutlets on a very hot barbecue 2 to 3 minutes a side, rest 3 minutes and serve with lemon.SweetsHalle and Claudia's pavlovaCrisp meringue shell, whipped cream and fresh passionfruitHow to make it4 Fold in the cornflour and vinegar.Shape into a round on baking paper.Bake at 120°C, then leave to cool in the oven with the door closed.Cool completely in the oven.Whip the cream and top the pavlova with cream, passionfruit, sliced kiwifruit and strawberries.DrinksHarbour passionfruit fizzSparkling wine, passionfruit pulp and elderflowerHow to make it1 bottle Australian sparkling wine (750 ml), chilled4 passionfruits60ml elderflower cordial4 sprigs of mintChill the flutes and the sparkling wine.Spoon passionfruit pulp into each glass with a measure of elderflower cordial.Top slowly with sparkling wine, stirring once to lift the pulp.
